principles.text: Make something people want: get real paying, retaining customers early and fundraising becomes easy.
User feedback is worthless until people pay or change behavior; people are polite and will lie to you.
Timebox each product-market hypothesis (reachable people plus a problem) so you get to try more of them.
Push fuzzy judgment into markdown skills and must-be-perfect work into code; keep the harness thin.
When you can't raise, try getting profitable before you sell, shut down or recap.

sampleQA.question: Should I raise a big round or stay lean?

answer.text: Raise big only if elite investors back you. Otherwise start lean, because lean is how you earn the right to go fat.
Money is gasoline on a fire that already exists. If you think you have a funding problem, you likely have a "people don't want it yet" problem.
In a hard market, aim for profitability or cash-flow break-even. $10M profit reinvested is like an annual Series A with no dilution.

sampleQA.question: How should a small team use AI agents?

answer.text: Treat AI as a workforce, not autocomplete. The same model gives 2x or 100x depending on how you wire the work.
Do a task once with the agent, turn it into a markdown skill, and run it on a cron. If you have to ask twice, you failed.
Get to 80-90% test coverage. Untested agent output shipped to users is slop.
Say what it is and who it's for. Don't be clever if clever means confusing.
Pick one high-contrast call to action and demote everything else to links.
Ask existing users how they describe your product and put their exact phrase at the top. For AI products, show a feat of strength.
